overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 28
overview.text: In this signature modeling lesson, you will apply algebra to real-world civic finance: the United States progressive income tax system. You will discover that tax brackets represent a continuous, piecewise linear function where each higher rate applies only to income within that specific marginal bracket.
outcomes: Calculate taxable income from gross income by accounting for standard deductions and exemptions.
Model marginal progressive taxation using piecewise linear functions $T(x)$.
Explain the critical difference between marginal tax rate and effective average tax rate.
overview.teacherInsight: Dispel the pervasive public myth that entering a higher tax bracket reduces net take-home pay. Progressive tax brackets are marginal: only the dollars earned ABOVE the bracket threshold are taxed at the higher percentage!

vocabulary.definition: The tax rate applied to the last dollar of income earned within a specific bracket.
The actual percentage of total income paid in taxes: (Total Tax Paid / Total Income) * 100%.
The amount of gross income used to calculate tax liability, after subtracting allowable exemptions and deductions.

practiceQuestions.question: An actress earns $\$10,000,000$ in gross income with married standard deductions of $\$12,200$ and exemptions of $\$7,800$. What is her taxable income?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
From the official Eureka Math Exit Ticket Key:
$\text{Taxable Income} = \$10,000,000 - (\$7,800 + \$12,200) = \$10,000,000 - \$20,000 = \$9,980,000$.

practiceQuestions.question: If her total federal income tax is $\$3,899,726$ on a gross income of $\$10,000,000$, what is her effective federal tax rate?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Effective tax rate is total tax paid divided by total gross income: $\frac{3,899,726}{10,000,000} \times 100\% \approx 38.997\% \approx 39.0\%$. Notice the effective rate is slightly lower than the top marginal tax bracket of $39.6\%$ due to graduated lower brackets.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 28 Exit Ticket: Federal Income Tax
exitTicket.prompt: A famous movie actress made $10 million last year. She is married with no children, and her husband earns no income. Compute her taxable income using: (taxable income) = (income) - (exemptions) - (standard deductions), with $7,800 exemptions and $12,200 deductions. Calculate her federal income tax using the 39.6% top bracket over $450,000, and find her effective tax rate.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Modeling Progressive Federal Income Tax Brackets
guidedExercises.problem:
Consider a simplified federal progressive tax bracket for single filers:
- 10% on taxable income from $\$0$ to $\$10,000$
- 15% on taxable income from $\$10,000$ to $\$40,000$
- 25% on taxable income over $\$40,000$
Calculate the federal tax owed on a taxable income of $\$55,000$, and compute the effective tax rate.
guidedExercises.scaffolding: Each tax rate applies ONLY to the income within its specific bracket range, not the total income.

steps.label: Compute total tax and effective tax rate
steps.explanation: Effective tax rate is overall percentage paid.

guidedExercises.commonPitfall: The widespread misconception that earning $\$55,000$ causes your entire salary to be taxed at 25% ($0.25 \times 55,000 = \$13,750$). Marginal tax rates only apply to the dollars inside that specific bracket!
